summary: 34-year-old man with four months of blood mixed with stool, looser stools, 6 kg weight loss and Hb 11.1, previously told he had piles. NICE NG12 (under 50 with rectal bleeding plus CIBH, weight loss or IDA): consider suspected cancer referral; colonoscopy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Bleeding from the back passage for four months
inputs.hpi: Four months of blood mixed in with the stool, darker than before, and looser stools 3 times a day. Lost 6 kg. Told by a clinic in January that it was piles and given a cream; no better. No family history known (adopted). No travel.

exam.other: PR: small external skin tag, no palpable mass, dark blood on the glove.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Rectal bleeding with change in bowel habit and weight loss — colorectal cancer to be excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Rectal bleeding mixed with stool, change in bowel habit, weight loss and iron-deficiency anaemia at 34. Not explained by the skin tag. Colonoscopy.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: consider suspected cancer referral in adults under 50 with rectal bleeding and any of abdominal pain, change in bowel habit, weight loss, IDA
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: ACPGBI/BSG joint guideline — FIT in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer
guideline.section: FIT is not a rule-out in patients with persisting concerning symptoms
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Davies MM, Abulafi M, et al. Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer (CRC): a joint guideline from the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI) and the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG). Gut. 2022;71:1939–1962.

rationale: Permutation: young age with a previous benign label. Rules keyed on age ≥ 50 (web "Rectal bleeding, age ≥ 50" prompt) or ≥ 40 (triage cancer screen) cannot see him; the differential must still carry colorectal cancer.
